title: Standby - normal
shortDescription: Healthy idle waiting for thermostat call.
fullDescription: Frigidaire HVAC furnaces (FG7T*, FT4B series, made by Nordyne) use the standard Nordyne control board. A slow steady single flash means healthy standby. If furnace doesn't start, check thermostat, batteries, low-voltage wiring, or blown fuse on IFC.
safetyWarning: Line voltage present at IFC even at idle.

fixSteps.title: Verify thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Check 24 V at R-W with heat call.

whenToCallPro: If 24 V good but no response.

faq.a: Same name, Nordyne licenses for HVAC.

title: Pressure switch stuck closed
fullDescription: Two flashes mean the IFC sees pressure switch closed before the inducer was commanded to start. Safety lockout.

title: Pressure switch failed to close
fullDescription: Three flashes typically mean clogged condensate trap, torn pressure hose, blocked vent, or weak inducer.

title: High limit open
fullDescription: Four flashes mean primary limit opened. Almost always restricted airflow - dirty filter, closed registers, slow blower.
safetyWarning: Repeated trips can mean cracked HX - CO hazard.

title: Roll-out switch tripped
fullDescription: Five flashes indicate roll-out limit opened. Critical safety event with CO risk.
safetyWarning: CO hazard - stop using and call tech.

title: Reverse polarity
fullDescription: Six flashes indicate polarity issue. Hire electrician.

faq.a: Flame sense uses ground for tiny rectified current.

title: Weak flame signal
fullDescription: Seven flashes mean burner lit but flame current too low. Clean flame sensor first.

title: Ignition failure
fullDescription: Eight flashes mean three full ignition trials failed. Hour lockout.

title: Phantom flame signal
fullDescription: Nine flashes - critical fault. Usually leaking gas valve.

title: Igniter / gas valve circuit fault
fullDescription: Ten flashes mean an open or shorted output to the igniter or gas valve.
symptoms: No igniter glow OR no gas response
